chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who marries a woman on the condition that she is a virgin, and he finds her to be non-virgin, is it permissible for him to keep her?
He (the Imam) said: 'The virgin is distinguished from the non-virgin by riding (sexual intercourse) and by penetration.'

And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Jazak, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who married a young virgin girl, and found her to be non-virgin, is the full dowry obligatory for her or is it reduced?

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And whoever marries a woman on the condition that he is free, and then it becomes apparent to her that he is a slave, she has the choice (to annul the marriage).

key_terms.ثَيِّبٌ: Non-virgin (previously married or known for sexual experience)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dowry reduction if a wife is found to be non-virgin after marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *al-tadlis* (deception) in marriage contracts, specifically regarding the material value of virginity (*bikr*) versus sexual availability (*nazwah*). Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes that while virginity is a distinct attribute verified through intercourse, its absence justifies a reduction in the dowry (*sadaq*) rather than automatic annulment, reflecting the Shia juristic view that virginity is a financial right rather than a condition of validity. The text also extends this principle to social status, granting the wife the right of option (*khiyar*) if a free man is misrepresented as a slave.
